prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup
Asset type: one high-fidelity production-ready mobile landing page direction comp for SettleUp, 9:16 portrait mobile-web viewport.
Primary request: Design “The Field Note Constellation,” a shippable phone-first landing page for a real product that turns bank transactions into friend-group expenses. It must read unmistakably as a practical responsive website screen, not a poster, editorial illustration, or photograph of a device.
Page structure from top to bottom: a restrained mobile header with wordmark on the left and a compact secondary action on the right; a clear hero headline and one large primary CTA; then one dominant interactive-looking focal composition where a real bank charge is pinned like a field specimen beside a hand-plotted map of the friend group; at the bottom edge, visibly continue a dotted field-path downward to hint that scrolling follows the journey from account to friends to settled balance. Show only enough below the fold to signal continuation, not a second competing hero.
Subject/content: the bank transaction is the product’s center of gravity. Make the transaction “Luna Pizza · $84.20” large and legible on a folded cream paper specimen slip, pinned with a small terracotta marker. Beside it, show an airy, countable social map with three clearly labeled nodes: “Jamie, Noor, Eli”, connected by hand-plotted lines and restrained map symbols. A precise dotted path visually connects the charge to the group, then continues beyond the viewport toward settlement. The UI must feel operable, with obvious button affordances, generous tap targets, clear hierarchy, and accessible contrast.
Style/medium: naturalist field journals blended with hand-plotted social maps; soft pencil lines, subtle map symbols, specimen labels, folded paper, fine imperfect registration, and restrained tactile paper grain. Notion-like usability: calm, practical, spacious, editorial but interface-first. Keep the header and controls clean and modern so the field-note material feels purposeful rather than themed decoration.
Composition/framing: exact straight-on full-bleed 9:16 portrait webpage screenshot, no phone frame, no hand holding a device, no surrounding scene. Use a single-column mobile grid with approximately 24px side margins. Header occupies about 8% of height, copy and CTA about 26%, transaction-to-friends focal composition about 48%, and scroll-path continuation about 18%. The transaction specimen and friend map form one integrated hero interaction, not separate generic cards.
Color palette: warm cream #EEE8DA background, near-black #292824 text and pencil work, terracotta #B86B45 for the primary CTA and specimen pin, muted sage #8F9278 for secondary lines and friend nodes. No gradients.
Materials/textures: softly fibrous uncoated paper, faint pencil, one subtle folded-paper edge; tactile but crisp enough for production UI. Avoid excessive scrapbook clutter.
Text (verbatim): Use only these exact visible strings, with exact capitalization and punctuation: “SettleUp”; “Find the charge. Share the story.”; “Connect a bank”; “Sign in”; “Luna Pizza · $84.20”; “Jamie, Noor, Eli”.
Typography: large confident near-black headline, humanist editorial sans or gently rounded grotesk; controls remain crisp and readable. All text must be correctly spelled, comfortably sized, and high contrast.
Constraints: Exactly one mobile landing page comp. Preserve all six required strings verbatim and introduce no other visible words, numbers, labels, claims, navigation items, metadata, or placeholder copy. Make “Connect a bank” the terracotta primary button and “Sign in” the compact header action. The landing page must communicate account-to-friends-to-settlement through visual path and layout only, without extra copy.
Avoid: invented claims, statistics, testimonials, partner logos, stock photos, photoreal people, generic dashboard cards, glassmorphism, gradients, neon colors, excessive shadows, illegible microtext, fake handwriting text, watermarks, decorative borders around the entire page, browser chrome, device mockups, poster composition.
